editorial:
Blood on the Sun is a 1945 film directed by Frank Lloyd. James Cagney plays Nick Condon. Wikipedia says the film is based on a fictional history behind the Tanaka Memorial document. William Cagney is listed as producer and United Artists as distributor. Miklós Rózsa is credited for the music, and Garrett Fort and Lester Cole are credited as writers. I did not check how the screenplay and story credits are split between them.

The rights question is unresolved. Wikipedia and an Internet Archive uploader's description say the copyright was not renewed. Both are secondhand claims, and I have not verified them. I did not read the Catalog of Copyright Entries Motion Pictures volumes for 1972, 1973 or 1974, and I did not search the Copyright Office public records. Check those before relying on public-domain status. The Rózsa score and any source material for the story have not been checked separately. Any restoration or re-release would add its own material.
faq: Is Blood on the Sun in the public domain?

Unverified. Wikipedia says the copyright was not renewed in the 28th year, and an Internet Archive uploader describes the film as public domain for lack of renewal. I did not check the 1972, 1973 or 1974 Catalog of Copyright Entries Motion Pictures volumes or the Copyright Office public records. Check them yourself before relying on this.
Can I use the Internet Archive copies and the Rózsa score?

Both Internet Archive pages load and show this film, but I did not check the source or quality of either copy. I did not check whether the Rózsa score has its own registration or renewal. Treat the score, and any added material in a particular copy, as uncleared until you check.
